briefing.headline: Which shop release is actually running?
briefing.summary: The team wants to confirm which version of the ${environment} shop service is deployed.

application.action: Find the ${environment} shop release in Applications and open it.
application.reason: The list contains more than one environment. Confirming the Application first keeps every later observation tied to the right release.
application.learning: This Application is the release whose status we were asked to verify.

health.action: Read the health badge in the Application header.
health.reason: The header gives the current workload state; a Git commit by itself says nothing about whether the workload is healthy.
health.learning: The health badge is the current workload signal. Keep it separate from the sync status and Git revision.

revision.action: Open History and Rollback and read the most recent deployed revision.
revision.reason: History ties an Argo sync event to a commit, so we can distinguish the deployed version from the latest branch tip.
revision.learning: History identifies the revision Argo applied. This is the commit to quote in a release status update.

briefing.headline: Verify the shop workload's readiness check
briefing.summary: The team wants to confirm the readiness endpoint for the ${environment} shop service.

deployment.action: Open the Application tree and find its Deployment node.
deployment.reason: The tree shows resources owned by this Application. Start there to avoid inspecting an unrelated workload in the same cluster.
deployment.learning: The Deployment in the tree is the workload Argo will reconcile for this release.

readiness-path.action: Open the Deployment's Manifest tab, select Desired, and read readinessProbe.httpGet.path.
readiness-path.reason: Desired is the rendered configuration Argo intends to apply. It is the right place to verify the probe before judging live pod behavior.
readiness-path.learning: The Desired manifest records the readiness path that new pods will receive on the next reconciliation.

briefing.headline: Confirm what Argo CD deployed
briefing.summary: Release Engineering wants to confirm which version reached the ${environment} shop service.

deployed-revision.action: Open History and Rollback and read the latest deployed revision.
deployed-revision.reason: History records the revision associated with the deployment, rather than only the revision currently visible in Git.
deployed-revision.learning: This revision is the deployment Argo recorded for the shop Application.

last-operation.action: Open Sync Status and inspect the latest operation phase.
last-operation.reason: A revision in History needs its operation result. The operation panel shows whether the apply completed or stopped partway through.
last-operation.learning: The operation phase tells us whether the latest sync finished successfully.

briefing.headline: Shop pods are failing to start
briefing.summary: New ${environment} shop pods are failing to start after a release.

application.action: Find the unhealthy ${environment} shop Application in Applications.
application.reason: Production and staging are both present. The environment label and health badge identify the release that needs evidence before any edit.
application.learning: The affected Application is now scoped; inspect only resources that belong to it.

missing-name.action: Open the failing Pod in the Application tree and read its Events tab.
missing-name.reason: A pod that cannot start often has a specific Kubernetes warning. Events can identify a missing dependency that the Application health badge cannot.
missing-name.learning: The warning names the dependency the pod could not load. Compare that name with the Deployment template in Git before editing it.

repair.action: Restore a valid ConfigMap reference in the Deployment template, commit and push it, then watch Argo reconcile.
repair.reason: The pod warning points to a dependency in desired state. Changing the chart in Git makes the repair survive Argo's next reconciliation.

briefing.headline: The shop release is still progressing
briefing.summary: The ${environment} shop release has not finished syncing, and its new pods are not ready.

application.action: Find the ${environment} shop Application and check that its release is still progressing.
application.reason: The Applications list establishes which environment is affected before we inspect or terminate a sync operation.
application.learning: This is the release whose readiness problem is holding the sync open.

probe-path.action: Open Deployment/django from the tree, then read readinessProbe.httpGet.path in its Desired manifest.
probe-path.reason: A Progressing badge only reports the symptom. The Desired manifest reveals the probe path Argo will keep applying to every new pod.
probe-path.learning: The configured path cannot answer the expected readiness request. A retry alone will reproduce the same unready pods.

repair.action: Terminate the operation that cannot finish in Sync Status, correct the probe path in Git, then let Argo sync the new commit.
repair.reason: The running operation must clear before another sync, and the probe must change in Git so reconciliation does not restore the bad value.

briefing.headline: The shop rollout stopped before its Deployment updated
briefing.summary: The ${environment} shop rollout stopped before its Deployment updated.

application.action: Find the blocked ${environment} shop Application in Applications.
application.reason: Scope the release before investigating its hooks; the other environment may have completed normally.
application.learning: This is the Application whose operation needs inspection.

hook.action: Open Sync Status and read the failed hook entry and phase.
hook.reason: The operation panel orders the sync stages. It tells us whether the failure happened before the Deployment could update.
hook.learning: The failed phase runs before the main apply, so the rollout cannot advance until that hook succeeds.

log.action: Open the failed migration Job in the tree and read its Logs tab.
log.reason: The phase identifies where the sync stopped; the Job's own output explains why the hook exited.
log.learning: The log line is the direct failure evidence to carry into the Git repair and incident note.

repair.action: Repair the migration hook in Git, commit and push it, then resync the Application.
repair.reason: The hook is part of desired release configuration; a manual retry without a source change will run the same failing step.

briefing.headline: A workload rename left the shop service without endpoints
briefing.summary: A workload rename left the ${environment} shop service with no ready endpoints.

application.action: Find the ${environment} shop Application and open its resource tree.
application.reason: A prune affects Application-owned resources. Confirm ownership and environment before considering a delete.
application.learning: The affected Application owns the resources we need to compare.

orphan.action: In the tree, find the Deployment marked as extra or requiring prune.
orphan.reason: The tree puts desired and leftover resources side by side. The extra node is evidence of the rename, not permission to delete every unhealthy resource.
orphan.learning: That Deployment remains from the earlier name. Compare Service selectors and the desired Deployment before pruning it.

repair.action: Restore a matching Service selector and Deployment in Git; inspect Diff, then prune only the leftover Deployment.
repair.reason: Fixing the selector restores endpoints, and a targeted prune removes the orphan without deleting the intended workload.

briefing.headline: The encrypted shop configuration will not render
briefing.summary: Argo CD cannot render the ${environment} shop release after an encrypted configuration update.

application.action: Find the ${environment} Application with a comparison error.
application.reason: Comparison errors appear before resource health can be judged. Locate the affected release without relying on a rendered tree.
application.learning: This Application is blocked before Argo can compare the new manifests.

cause.action: Open Conditions and read the manifest generation error.
cause.reason: When rendering fails, a Pod Events tab may not exist for the new revision. Conditions carry the source error returned by manifest generation.
cause.learning: The condition identifies the decryption component that prevents Argo from rendering the encrypted source.

repair.action: Re-encrypt the secret from known plaintext in the lab terminal, commit and push the encrypted file, then wait for Argo to compare it.
repair.reason: A damaged encrypted data key cannot be repaired by retrying sync. A valid encrypted source lets manifest generation resume.

briefing.headline: Encrypted values failed an integrity check
briefing.summary: Argo CD cannot render the latest encrypted ${environment} shop configuration.

application.action: Find the ${environment} shop Application with the comparison error.
application.reason: A render failure can look similar to other source failures in the list. First tie the error to the correct release.
application.learning: This is the Application whose desired manifests could not be produced.

cause.action: Open Conditions and find the integrity field named by the error.
cause.reason: Conditions hold the manifest generation message. Naming the field distinguishes a whole-file integrity mismatch from a missing decryption key.
cause.learning: The named integrity field explains why SOPS rejected the file before Argo could render the chart.

repair.action: Recover the known values in the terminal and re-encrypt the file with a fresh integrity value, then commit and push.
repair.reason: The integrity record must match the encrypted values. Re-running sync against the same file cannot make them agree.

briefing.headline: An encrypted value blocked the shop release
briefing.summary: Argo CD cannot render the ${environment} shop release after an encrypted values update.

application.action: Find the ${environment} Application with the comparison error.
application.reason: The list separates the failed release from the healthy one before we inspect the encrypted source.
application.learning: This is the release whose manifest generation is blocked.

cause.action: Open Conditions and read the error for the encrypted value.
cause.reason: The condition text distinguishes a value authentication failure from a missing key or a whole-file integrity mismatch.
cause.learning: The encrypted value failed authentication, so the repair needs known plaintext and fresh encryption.

repair.action: Re-encrypt the known-good plaintext value in the terminal, commit the encrypted file, and let Argo compare the new revision.
repair.reason: Authentication verifies the encrypted value itself. A retry or skipped integrity check cannot supply valid ciphertext.

briefing.headline: The latest secrets change blocked the release
briefing.summary: An encrypted secrets change is blocking the ${environment} shop release.

application.reason: Scope the release first; the failure may surface as a comparison condition or as a failed operation.
application.learning: This is the Application whose encrypted update needs investigation.

cause.action: Read Conditions or Sync Status and identify the values key named by the error.
cause.reason: The error's stage tells us whether the chart failed to render or the rendered resources failed to apply. Its key points to the input to inspect.
cause.learning: The named key has the wrong shape for the chart. Fix the encrypted source before trying another sync.

repair.action: Re-encrypt a valid secrets map in the terminal, commit and push it; clear any failed operation so Argo can sync.
repair.reason: The chart expects key-value secrets. Editing the encrypted source makes the corrected shape durable.

briefing.headline: One shop environment is unhealthy
briefing.summary: The ${environment} shop release is unhealthy while the other environment is working.

application.action: Compare the two shop cards in Applications and open the unhealthy ${environment} release.
application.reason: The healthy peer is a control case. Its status helps narrow the issue to environment-specific configuration.
application.learning: The failing release is scoped to one environment; compare its desired configuration with the healthy peer.

probe-path.action: Open the failing Deployment's Desired manifest and read readinessProbe.httpGet.path.
probe-path.reason: The healthy peer narrows the scope to one environment. The failing release's Desired manifest shows the exact probe Argo keeps applying there.
probe-path.learning: The path in the failing release is the setting to compare with the healthy environment's source before making a scoped edit.

repair.action: Restore the affected environment's readiness path in its Git values file, commit and push, then verify Argo's new revision.
repair.reason: The healthy environment is evidence for the expected setting. A scoped Git edit preserves the working release.

briefing.headline: Argo CD cannot fetch the shop source
briefing.summary: Argo CD cannot fetch the source for the ${environment} shop release.

application.action: Find the ${environment} Application with a source or comparison error.
application.reason: A source failure can leave old pods running. The Applications list shows which release has lost reconciliation even if health still looks acceptable.
application.learning: This is the Application whose source connection needs investigation.

source.action: Open Conditions and read the repository URL and transport in the error.
source.reason: A repository fetch failure occurs before manifests can be compared. Conditions distinguish access to source from a broken chart or workload.
source.learning: The failing transport points to an Application source setting. Compare it with the working repository entry before changing credentials or URL.

working-source.action: Open Settings → Repositories and inspect the connected Gitea entry.
working-source.reason: We need a known-good URL and transport before editing the Application source. The repository entry shows the connection Argo can already use.
working-source.learning: The connected repository uses a different transport from the failing Application. Restore the source URL to match that working entry.

repair.action: Compare the Application source with the working repository entry, restore its authenticated URL, and refresh the Application.
repair.reason: The error is in source access, so changing workload manifests would not help Argo fetch the repository.

repair.finding: The workload recovered after Argo synced the fix.

revision.why: History records the Git commit Argo actually deployed.

deployment.why: The tree lists the workload owned by this Application.

readiness-path.why: Desired shows the probe path Argo will apply to new pods.

deployed-revision.why: History records the Git commit Argo actually deployed.

last-operation.why: Sync Status shows whether Argo finished applying that revision.

application.what: Find and click the ${application} card in Applications.
application.why: Its status identifies the release with pods failing to start.

missing-name.what: Open ${application} → Tree → failing Pod → Events; read the ConfigMap name.
missing-name.why: The Pod warning names the missing dependency blocking startup.

repair.what: Restore the ConfigMap reference in the Deployment template, then push the Git change.
repair.why: The Pod Event names the dependency the desired Deployment must reference.

application.what: In Applications, find and click ${application} after checking its sync status.
application.why: The card identifies the ${environment} release whose sync has not settled.

probe-path.what: Open ${application} → Tree → Deployment/django → Manifest → Desired; read readinessProbe.httpGet.path.
probe-path.why: Desired shows the probe path Argo keeps applying to new pods.

repair.what: Terminate the operation in Sync Status, fix the probe path in Git, then push.
repair.why: The old operation blocks a new sync, and the wrong path keeps pods unready.

application.why: The card identifies the ${environment} release blocked before its Deployment updated.

hook.what: Open ${application} → Sync Status; read the failed hook phase.
hook.why: The operation list shows which hook stopped the rollout.

log.what: Open ${application} → Tree → migration Job → Logs; read the failure line.
log.why: The Job log explains why the PreSync hook exited.

repair.what: Fix the migration hook in Git, push the commit, then resync ${application}.
repair.why: The failed PreSync Job must succeed before the Deployment can update.

application.what: Find and click the ${application} card in Applications.
application.why: The card identifies the Application that owns the affected service.

orphan.what: Open ${application} → Tree; inspect the Deployment marked for pruning.
orphan.why: The tree separates the leftover Deployment from the desired workload.

repair.what: Fix the Service selector in Git, then prune the leftover Deployment in Argo.
repair.why: Matching selectors restore endpoints; targeted pruning removes only the old workload.

application.what: In Applications, find and click ${application} with the comparison error.
application.why: The card identifies the release Argo cannot render.

cause.what: Open ${application} → Conditions; read the SOPS decryption error.
cause.why: Conditions contains the manifest generation error before a resource tree exists.

repair.what: Re-encrypt the affected secret in the terminal, then commit and push it.
repair.why: Conditions shows Argo cannot decrypt the current file.

application.what: In Applications, find and click ${application} with the comparison error.
application.why: The card identifies the release Argo cannot render.

cause.what: Open ${application} → Conditions; read the SOPS integrity field in the error.
cause.why: Conditions names the field that failed validation during manifest generation.

repair.what: Re-encrypt the secret with a fresh integrity value, then push the Git change.
repair.why: The SOPS integrity record must match the encrypted values Argo reads.

application.what: In Applications, find and click ${application} with the comparison error.
application.why: The card identifies the release Argo cannot render.

cause.what: Open ${application} → Conditions; read the error for the encrypted value.
cause.why: Conditions distinguishes this value failure from missing keys or whole-file errors.

repair.what: Re-encrypt the affected value from known plaintext, then push the Git change.
repair.why: The value needs valid ciphertext before Argo can render manifests.

application.what: In Applications, find and click ${application}, the blocked release.
application.why: The card identifies which ${environment} deployment cannot reconcile.

cause.what: Open ${application} → Conditions or Sync Status; read the values key in the error.
cause.why: That error names the input that failed to render or apply.

repair.what: Re-encrypt a valid secrets map in the terminal, then push and resync.
repair.why: The chart expects a map; the current encrypted value has the wrong shape.

application.what: Compare the shop Applications, then click ${application}.
application.why: Their status cards show the failure is limited to ${environment}.

repair.what: Correct the ${environment} readiness path in its Git values file, then push.
repair.why: The working environment provides the expected path without a shared chart change.

application.what: In Applications, find and click ${application} with the source error.
application.why: The card identifies the release whose desired state cannot be fetched.

source.why: Conditions shows which source address Argo failed to fetch.

working-source.what: Open Settings → Repositories; read the connected Gitea URL and transport.
working-source.why: The connected entry shows a repository address Argo can already use.

repair.what: Restore ${application}'s repository URL to the working Gitea address, then refresh.
repair.why: Conditions and Repositories reveal the failing transport and the working URL.
